body: U4 resolver half opened as PR 198, branch fix/resolve-conflict-enumerates-every-field, commit e3fd3499, based on 63eb63ce and targeting main. Not merged; CI in flight. Three files: src/server/tools/resolve_conflict.ts, test/sync/resolve.test.ts, test/unit/resolve-conflict-fields.test.ts. No CRITICAL and no HIGH from code-reviewer, conformance-auditor or security-reviewer.U+000AU+000ATHE FOUR-SITES CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS NOW CORRECTED. The risk recorded from U3 said only the field pattern fails loudly if forgotten. Two of the four are loud, not one, and the two silent ones are worse than the record implied.U+000AU+000AU+002D INDEXED_FIELD_PATTERN: nothing matches, applyThreadField returns null, unclassifiableFieldRefusal. Loud.U+000AU+002D applyThreadField: falls through every branch to return null, same refusal. LOUD, contrary to the recorded risk.U+000AU+002D currentThreadFieldValue: the staleness guard reads if (lookup.recognized && !isDeepStrictEqual(...)), so an unrecognised lookup short-circuits the guard entirely and the winner is applied with no refusal, overwriting a local change. Silent, and a data-loss path.U+000AU+002D escapeChosenThreadValue: the unmatched fallback returns the value, so an artifact's label and pointer reach storage unescaped, and ThreadRecord.parse checks length and pattern rather than escaping, so it commits. Silent.U+000AU+000AVerified independently by the implementer and the code reviewer against the pre-fix code. The derivation closes both silent paths structurally: currentThreadFieldValue and applyThreadField now gate on the same two predicates in the same order, so no field exists for which apply succeeds while lookup returns unrecognised.U+000AU+000ATWO MORE CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF. A test file for this tool already existed at test/sync/resolve.test.ts, 448 lines with spawned-server fixtures; the brief claimed none. The behavioural red-on-parent tests went there to reuse those fixtures, and the censuses went into a new test/unit/resolve-conflict-fields.test.ts as the lowest layer expressing them. Separately the indexed pattern previously accepted an optional spine. prefix, so a bare open_risks[id] matched; deriving from THREAD_RULES drops that, and every historical version of field-merge.ts was checked to confirm no version ever emitted the bare form.U+000AU+000ARECEIPTS AS REPORTED. typecheck exit 0; npm test 805 pass, 0 fail, with both known intermittents passing in that run. Red on parent was behavioural, not just a compile error: a fixture drove a real conflict through the merge engine via a real sync_ledger call on two spawned teammates and hit the real handler, producing 'names a field this tool does not know how to apply: spine.landed' and the same for artifacts. The lead did not re-run the implementer's checks, by the delegation rule, and labelled its own status on them as read-from-receipt rather than observed.U+000AU+000AFILED ABOVE THE CEILING, NOT FOLDED IN. escapeCriterion escapes text only, while Criterion.check and Criterion.result are content-classed and pass through raw; pre-existing, not introduced here, not exploitable today because every render surface escapes at read time. THREAD_RULES is imported as a value but used only in type positions under verbatimModuleSyntax, so the file carries a runtime dependency nothing reads.U+000AU+000AONE COSMETIC NOTE. The commit subject is 74 characters, above the 72 pr-title-lint enforces, but the PR title is 70 and was accepted, and GitHub seeds the squash subject from the title, so nothing is at risk.
